newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks retreat slightly mid week.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks retreat slightly mid week.

text.p: Cyprus shares retreated slightly in listless mid-week trading but analysts predicted a bull run towards the end of the year.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general index, which is set at 100 points, closed at 84.13, losing 0.79 percent, or 0.67 points from its close of 84.80 on Friday.
Banking stocks, which represent the bulk of transactions on the exchange, closed at 92.97, losing 1.02 points from 93.99 on Friday.
"I feel that the three main banks have room for further increases until the end of the year," said Stavros Agrotis of CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation.
"I think the drop in banking stocks is temporary. Most investors feel comfortable with banking shares so there is room for an increase," he said.

The Bank of Cyprus closed at 348.5, down six cents from Friday. Fully-paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank stood at 334.5, down half a cent from Friday's close of 335. Fully paid shares of Hellenic Bank lost 4.5 cents to close at 267.5.
Shares in the Universal Savings Bank closed at 134.5 from 136 on Friday.
Keo Ltd closed at 113, up from Friday's close and year low of 105 after announcing losses before tax of 393,000 pounds in the first half of the year.
The sub index of the insurance sector closed at 60.98 from 62.12 on Friday.

Universal Life Insurance closed at 386 from 379 on Friday. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid closed down seven cents from Friday at 136. Fully paid shares of Interamerican Insurance closed at 105.5, losing two cents from Friday's close of 107.5.

National carrier Cyprus Airways, which on Tuesday reported pre-tax losses of 2.9 million pounds in its half yearly results, saw its share price sink even lower to 39.5 cents, an all year low. The nominal price of its shares is 50 cents.
